studies.organism: Male and female mice at least seven weeks old, with assay-specific genetic lines
studies.preparation: Separate peripheral cytokine/LPS, cNST or nodose chemogenetic, vagotomy, high-dose endotoxin survival and live Salmonella infection preparations.
studies.observable: FOS, population or cellular calcium, blood cytokine ELISA, survival and tissue bacterial colony counts; transcript and tracer observations and assay-specific nulls
studies.finding: Peripheral challenges evoked neural readouts, while selected neural manipulations changed circulating cytokines. Activation improved high-dose endotoxin survival but increased bacterial tissue load in a different live-infection protocol. A complete descending immune circuit is not identified.
limitations: Both male and female mice at least seven weeks old were used; exact age and sex distributions per assay group are not supplied. No randomized animal allocation, blinded investigation or prospective statistical sample-size calculation is reported. The reporting summary discusses stimulus ordering separately; it does not establish randomized animal groups.

FOS labeling is an activity-associated marker; Vglut2-cre bulk GCaMP6s is a population calcium signal, not a DBH-specific spike recording. Photometry uses saline on day 4 and LPS on day 5 in the same animals. Vagotomized mice form a separate group after two weeks of recovery; a matched abdominal sham is not explicitly specified in the reviewed procedure. Figure 1c reports residual responses after an approximately 80% reduction.

LPS doses differ across assays: 50 micrograms/kg for FOS and TRAP, 0.5 mg/kg for the main photometry comparison, 0.1 mg/kg for cytokine chemogenetics and 12.5 mg/kg for survival. These exposures are not interchangeable. LPS endotoxaemia is distinct from viable bacterial infection.

Fos-based TRAP2 labeling is followed by at least four weeks before functional rechallenge to restore LPS sensitivity. LPS-TRAPed, Dbh-cre, Vglut2-cre and Vgat-cre populations are not identical. Dbh expression does not measure norepinephrine release or identify a unique molecular mediator.

For standard cytokine chemogenetics, Methods specify CNO at 2 mg/kg twelve hours and 1 mg/kg one hour before challenge; schematics and captions show only the one-hour pretreatment. mCherry controls receive CNO. Saline/LPS tests use the same cohort at least seven days apart, whereas hM3Dq/hM4Di versus mCherry comparisons use separate groups. Blood ELISA at two hours does not identify cytokine-producing cells.

Cre-defined nodose activation perturbs marker-defined neurons; it is not selective activation of the TRPA1 channel or CALCA peptide. TRPA1 neurons include different stimulus-responsive subgroups. Extended Data 8e shows two IL-10/fat co-responders among 63 neurons, which the authors did not consider further. Universal zero overlap is unsupported.

Injected cytokines and extraintestinal perfusion have different doses, routes and recording windows. The response classifier uses baseline median absolute deviation, a mean modified z-score above 1.6 and peak fluorescence of at least 1%. Selected, normalized responder heatmaps are not an unbiased full-population distribution. In vivo responses do not establish direct cytokine binding to a neuronal receptor; epithelial or immune intermediates remain possible. Referenced imaging procedures have not been fully audited.

Survival experiments use separate Trpa1-cre nodose and Dbh-cre cNST cohorts after high-dose LPS, with repeated 5 mg/kg CNO dosing. Figure 6 shows survival through nine days, not a lifelong or clinical outcome. Separate infection experiments use oral Salmonella and eight CNO injections beginning twelve hours before inoculation; bacterial load is measured in spleen and mesenteric lymph nodes at day five.

Nonsignificance is not equivalence or proof of no pathway contribution. The corticosterone null is a two-hour circulating concentration, not complete exclusion of hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal mediation. Extended Data 3 reuses the Figure 2c saline/LPS data; it is not an independent replication.

The cNST transcriptomic atlas pools tissue from five animals; 4,008 cells and expression clusters are not independent animal replicates, anatomical coordinates or a measured connectome. Rabies labeling supports an anatomical input interpretation, not synaptic efficacy. Main text calls the rabies reporter dsRed while Methods and Extended Data 12 specify GFP; panel 12d depicts Trpa1 but repeats Calca in its quantitative caption. No tracing fraction is calibrated.

Descending efferent routes and immune effector cells remain unresolved. A whole-animal Myd88 knockout does not isolate immune-cell-specific mediation. Lower circulating inflammatory cytokines do not imply universally better defense: sustained TRPA1-population activation increased Salmonella tissue burden in the separate live-infection assay.

Raw measurements, animal identifiers and custom code have not been obtained or replayed. Exclusion criteria include unsuccessful targeting/expression/ablation, but counts and operational thresholds are incomplete. Extended Data 9c reports Gpr65 IL-6 P=0.03 despite a broad no-appreciable-effect conclusion; its small plotted decrease must not be turned into an all-population null. No numerical edge weight or universal carrier count is assigned.

The DSS Methods specify CNO in the experimental cohort drinking solution, while Figure 6 says all animals received CNO. Matched control exposure and intake need resolution before a selective DSS mechanism is admitted. This issue does not change the separately described injected-CNO LPS or infection protocols.

studies.preparation: Isolated cEC patch clamp, pressurized capillary-arteriole preparations and separate anesthetized somatosensory imaging/flow experiments.
studies.observable: Kir currents, upstream membrane potential, vessel diameter, RBC flux and velocity, relative cortical perfusion and selected null controls
studies.finding: Capillary potassium evokes upstream dilation and hyperpolarization and increased RBC passage under specified conditions. Endothelial Kcnj2 deletion reduces the whisker perfusion response without eliminating it.
limitations: Adult male mice; Online Methods state two to three months, but Supplementary Table 2 reports mean ages of 14.8 weeks for C57BL/6 and 17.0 weeks for knockout laser-Doppler cohorts. No exact universal age range is admitted. No randomization, blinding, prospective sample-size calculation or exclusions were reported.

Kcnj2 deletion uses constitutive Tek-Cre, not adult-induced capillary-only deletion. Isolated cEC currents and control smooth-muscle currents support endothelial attribution but do not exclude developmental effects or establish restriction to one vascular segment. Identical listed genotyping primer pairs require verification before protocol reproduction.

Whole-cell currents are measured with 60 mM external potassium; this recording solution is distinct from 10 mM focal capillary stimulation, 15 mM cortical superfusion and physiological neural release. Kir2.1/Kcnj2 is the primary molecular identity. Ba2+ also blocks vascular Kir channels outside capillary endothelium.

CaPA is an isolated, pressurized preparation with sealed capillary ends, not normal flowing blood. Diameter, upstream smooth-muscle voltage and in vivo flux come from separate recordings. Membrane-potential recordings use wortmannin to suppress movement. Estimated conduction speed is inferred from distance and onset, not voltage measured along every endothelial cell.

In vivo measurements use acute cranial windows and alpha-chloralose/urethane after isoflurane surgery. RBC flux is cells per second; velocity is distance per time; laser Doppler gives a relative tissue perfusion signal. None is BOLD, oxygen consumption or an exact anatomical network reconstruction.

Peak RBC flux is the maximum one-second bin in an approximately seventeen-second post-stimulus interval relative to about three seconds of baseline. Velocity is sampled in the peak-flux bin, not an independently selected peak. Paired observations and nested capillaries are not independent mice.

The Figure 4 diameter null concerns eighteen capillaries in seven mice; the authors state that sampled measurement sites lacked pericytes. Upstream diameter uses eight paired experiments in seven mice. The local null does not exclude pericyte effects at other segments or prove equivalence.

Whisker responses persist after endothelial Kcnj2 deletion. Surface barium has a broader target range and leaves residual perfusion responses. The potassium source during neural activity and the complete intercellular route remain unresolved; potassium ejection bypasses the physiological release step.

Supplementary Figure 5 reports five preparations but paired t statistics with five degrees of freedom; Figure 7 reports group sizes inconsistent with its unpaired-test degrees of freedom. Supplementary Table 1 and Table 2 also reverse control-line sample counts for the flow comparisons. Exact quantitative calibration requires animal-identified measurements and resolution.

Nonsignificance is not equivalence. The selected SK/IK activation protocols do not exclude every calcium-dependent endothelial channel. The LFP control tests selected spectral bands, not complete neural activity, and the TTX potassium experiment does not identify the physiological potassium-releasing cell.

Raw recordings and custom MATLAB LFP software have not been obtained or reproduced. The reporting checklist and main text do not provide a resolved access route. No numerical edge weights, universal minimal carrier counts or independently validated full pathway are assigned.

limitations: Wild-type C57BL/6J experiments use male mice aged three to four months. Genetic cohorts include males and females pooled after reported baseline comparisons; experimenters were blinded to genotype only. The stated birth-order randomization and counterbalancing do not specify the random sequence. Grubbs outlier exclusions and a greater-than-five-percent initial hyperemia inclusion rule are reported without a complete included/excluded-animal manifest.

Arf6iECKD is partial, inducible endothelial knockdown, with about thirty percent reduction attributed to the referenced characterization. Both genotypes receive tamoxifen, 2 mg per mouse daily for five days, followed by at least one month washout. It is not complete Arf6 loss or a capillary-only intervention.

The ATP-depletion assay uses mixed microvessel lysates, including endothelial cells, distal pericytes and astrocyte endfeet. Residual ATP is an inverse kinase-activity proxy under added substrate/cofactors, not direct membrane PIP2 concentration. GTPgammaS is not selective for Arf6. Results give 0.012% DMSO whereas Methods give 0.01%; exact solvent concentration needs resolution.

NAV-2729 is pharmacological and not exclusively Arf6-selective. Main Methods describe additional GEF/GAP targets in overlapping concentration ranges. Genetic comparisons and supplementation constrain interpretation but do not identify a unique PIP2-mediated route or exclude effects in other neurovascular cells.

Whole-cell currents use 60 mM external potassium and are measured separately from focal 10 mM capillary stimulation. For pharmacological protection, bath diC16-PIP2 is present before recording; it is not a sequential rescue of the same cell after current loss. Repeated ramps and cells nested within mice do not provide independent animal replications.

Myography pools pressure-induced tone and U46619 preconstriction; it measures upstream diameter, not propagated membrane voltage. The printed tone formula is prestimulated/maximal diameter, whereas the Results and Figure 3B describe constriction from maximal diameter. This normalization needs resolution before numerical reuse.

Laser Doppler responses are relative perfusion, not absolute flow, BOLD or spike rate. Manual whisker stimulation precludes estimating propagation kinetics. NAV or vehicle is superfused for twenty minutes; genetic PIP2 flow rescue is a separate cohort from the barium comparison, not a repeated rescue in the same animals.

Figure 4b reports four to seven animals for traces whereas Figure 4c reports six to eight for animal summaries. Technical trial counts also need reconciliation with the Methods average of three trials. The Ba2+-sensitive fraction in Figure 4f is normalized to the total response; the Methods subtraction formula omits that denominator. No precise fraction or dose-response fit is calibrated.

Vehicle alone increases the Figure 4c hyperemic response. Concurrent NAV/PIP2 preserves a response relative to its own baseline but does not fully restore the higher vehicle-treated response, as acknowledged in the Discussion. Nonsignificance between treated genotypes is not equivalence; no complete physiological rescue or clinical efficacy is established.

Separate supporting information, animal identifiers, raw recordings and analysis code remain unread or unavailable here. Main Figures 1-4 and Methods support scoped reported outcomes, not independent reproduction of data, exclusions, nesting or statistics. Supplemental genotype, blood-pressure, glucose and lower-dose controls are not independently admitted.

PIP2 availability is inferred from kinase and Kir current assays; the study does not directly quantify membrane lipid abundance or test all Arf6 pathways. Cross-preparation consistency does not prove that this is the sole mediator of blood-flow responses or a universal rule for constructing the graph.

limitations: Adult mice of both sexes, overall age range 8-41 weeks. BMX:CreERT2 Gja4fl/fl Gja5fl/fl animals and Cre-negative double-floxed controls both receive tamoxifen. The driver targets arterial endothelium beyond the brain, including aorta; it is not a capillary-only or brain-only intervention. Assay-specific age/sex distributions are not fully resolved.

No prospective sample-size calculation. Genotype-blinded functional imaging acquisition and randomized stimulus order are reported; random stimulus order is not random genotype allocation. Pre-unblinding exclusions lack a complete animal manifest. The Gja4 floxed allele has an oocyte hypomorphism; same-flox controls do not establish equivalence to wild-type physiology.

Aortic electrophysiology uses six cells from only two mice per genotype; tracer loading uses six control and eight mutant fills from two mice per genotype. Cell-level tests do not supply six or eight independent animals. Apparent capacitance includes the coupled network, not just one cell surface. These are aortic recordings, not brain endothelial voltage recordings.

Retinal SERT tracing uses viral overexpression and terminal transcardial serotonin loading under anesthesia, 6-9 weeks after tamoxifen. Large-artery spreading events require favorable loading and occurred in only two of four controls; single-cell fills occurred in all four mutants. This selected qualitative tracing cannot determine a population conductance or physiological serotonin pathway.

Cx37, Cx40, Cx43 and Cx45 reporter distributions describe vascular segments; expression alone does not measure coupling strength or signal direction. Small-vessel tracer persistence is qualitative. A two-gene arterial deletion does not isolate the function of each isoform or test a selective isoform swap.

Focal visual two-photon imaging measures relative diameter; widefield IOS measures an optical HbT-related response. Neither IOS nor the derived response-propagation speed is a calibrated blood-flow, RBC-velocity, oxygen-use or electrical-conduction measurement. General functional analyses select arteries with baseline diameter greater than 15 micrometers.

Visual activity distance uses normalized, thresholded widefield GCaMP, which is biased toward upper cortical layers. The threshold does not prove absence of deeper or sparse activity. Optogenetic distance instead uses a postmortem ChRmine-expression mask, not simultaneous firing measurements. Histological arterial masks are manually registered and refined, not generated causal geometry.

Motion, pupil and locomotion corrections and signal-selection rules affect the analyzed response. In two-photon processing, selected low-power traces are set to zero by an analysis rule. Linear mixed models account for nesting in functional comparisons; the separate resting-diameter test treats vessels as independent despite nesting within mice.

Optogenetic stimulation uses two-second ChRmine pulse trains and six mice per genotype. The zero-laser condition can retain spontaneous vasomotion and imaging-light opsin activation; it is not an opsin-negative control. Functional imaging days 14-16 after viral injection do not specify a universal post-tamoxifen interval.

Propagation velocity is derived from the inverse slope of optical-response onset time versus position along a selected artery, with onset at ten percent of a sigmoid fit. Figure 5E calls it the slope, whereas Methods specify the inverse. Velocity analysis reports thirty averaged repeats, while the general optogenetic protocol reports ninety per power across sessions; subset selection requires clarification.

Full-screen noise differs from focal circles in spatial coverage and pattern. The comparison does not isolate energetic demand, and oxygen consumption or ATP supply is not measured. Time-to-peak genotype differences depend on distance bin; the farthest optogenetic and full-field bins are nonsignificant, not evidence of equivalence.

Resting microvascular control measures capillary RBC velocity near 100 micrometers depth, not whole-brain perfusion or RBC flux. Tail-cuff systolic/diastolic pressure is a separate systemic control. Nonsignificance in these small cohorts does not demonstrate physiological equivalence.

PMC author-manuscript passages and the author-hosted in-press PDF were read, including main Figures 1-6 and supplementary Figures S5-S7. Selected Methods cover the admitted assays; general cloning/culture methods and remaining supplemental material were not fully audited. Final bibliographic pagination is 5003-5019.e22, whereas the read in-press PDF ends its Methods at e12; version completeness remains unresolved.

Separate statistical/genotyping Tables S1-S2, allele-map files and movies were not obtained or replayed. Raw measurements are available from the authors on request and have not been obtained. The paper identifies code DOI 10.7910/DVN/XRRGRI, but public repository access failed; code files were not inspected or executed. No numerical edge weights or independent experimental reproduction are claimed.

Aortic electrical measurements, retinal tracer spread and awake cortical responses are distinct preparations. Cerebral endothelial voltage is not recorded along the full route. Gap junctions can carry small molecules as well as current; residual vascular responses and alternative routes prevent identification of a unique complete neural-to-vascular mechanism.

studies.preparation: Retroviral dividing-cell labeling after standard or running housing; fixed-tissue morphology and runner-only hippocampal slice electrophysiology.
studies.observable: Neuronal markers, morphology, BrdU counts, current-evoked spikes, spontaneous and evoked postsynaptic responses and passive electrical properties.
studies.finding: Selected birth-labeled neurons acquire neuronal morphology and electrophysiological responses. Input integration is supported in this preparation; unbiased generation rates, mature output transmission and memory necessity are not tested.
limitations: Female C57BL/6 mice were four to five weeks old at housing allocation and received virus one week later. Birth labeling therefore starts at approximately five to six weeks, not uniformly in fully mature adults. Electrophysiology was four to eight weeks after injection and used runners only.

Retroviral GFP labels a selected dividing-cell population. Variable infection, neuronal GFP downregulation and faint cells prevent absolute neurogenesis-rate estimation. BrdU incorporation is a separate DNA-labeling assay; a 48-hour count is not a count of mature functional neurons.

Of 58 recorded GFP-positive cells, 13 from 13 mice had neuronal physiology; 45 were nonexcitable and not all individually identified. The 13/58 fraction is a selected recording yield, not an unbiased neuronal differentiation probability. Unlabeled comparison neurons were not birthdated.

Sample sizes vary by assay and parameter. Table 3 compares up to 13 labeled neurons and 27 unlabeled neurons from 23 mice; cell nesting is not a fully reconstructed animal-level analysis. Randomized housing allocation, blinding and a prospective sample-size calculation are not reported in the reviewed Methods.

Spontaneous postsynaptic responses were seen in six labeled neurons, and perforant-path-evoked responses in four. Selective transmitter blockade is not supplied for every input. The paired-pulse example does not establish a universal sign rule, and afferent input is not direct proof of output transmission to CA3.

Table 3 nonsignificant comparisons are not equivalence tests. The membrane time constant differs, and capacitance is calculated from time constant/input resistance rather than measured as a direct morphological quantity.

The four-week and four-month morphology samples contain different cells. Eight cells are used per age for most measures, with five for four-month spine density; their animal distribution is not resolved. This is not longitudinal tracking of the same dendrite.

Running and standard housing have separate BrdU samples of five and four mice. Housing is a multicomponent exposure, not a selective learning manipulation. Normal adult neurogenesis does not thereby require training or tissue injury.

Main experimental text, Methods, Figures 1-5 captions and Tables 1-3 were read in the PMC author manuscript; Figures 3-5 were visually inspected. Raw recordings, animal-identified data and the LabVIEW acquisition code were not obtained or replayed.

No behavioral memory test or selective newborn-neuron ablation is performed here. Cell birth labeling, neuronal markers, synaptic morphology, input responses and cognitive necessity are distinct claims.

studies.preparation: Frozen dentate-gyrus-enriched tissue, paired single-nucleus RNA and ATAC sequencing, reference-assisted annotation and cross-sectional cohort comparisons.
studies.observable: Molecular cell labels, inferred trajectories and normalized cell-type abundance; selected publisher workbook counts and reported contrasts.
studies.finding: Molecular profiles are consistent with candidate neurogenic populations and vary across cohorts. Unresolved cohort counts, annotation assumptions and observational design prevent a birth-rate or causal memory conclusion.
limitations: Cross-sectional postmortem hippocampal samples compare young adults (YA), healthy agers (HA), preclinical intermediate pathology (PCI), Alzheimer disease (AD) and SuperAgers (SA). There is no randomized diagnosis, in vivo birthdating, lineage follow-up, electrophysiology or neurogenesis intervention.

The main text reports 38 participants, including eight HA, whereas both cohort-table sheets and the abundance workbook contain 39 sample IDs, including nine HA. Identical demographic/pathology fields occur for some different IDs; this does not prove duplicate donors. The donor/sample manifest and independence remain unresolved.

Table 8 filter_counts contains 153530 retained nuclei across 39 samples. The paper reports 355997 sequenced nuclei. These are different processing stages, not an established count contradiction; a complete retained/excluded-nucleus manifest has not been reconstructed.

Rare cell labels depend on quality filtering, reference-assisted annotation, marker expression and model-based trajectory inference. RNA-velocity latent time is not elapsed lineage time. A UMAP embedding is not measured physical tissue geometry.

The abundance analysis uses per-sample counts and library-size normalization, not absolute whole-hippocampus numbers or neuron birth rates. Published log-fold changes and adjusted P values are retained as reported comparisons; edgeR analysis and sequencing data have not been rerun.

SuperAgers come from Northwestern, while the other groups come from the University of Washington. Tissue source, individual variability and clinical selection can confound group comparisons. The Methods and main text differ in their reference age wording for SuperAger memory criteria; a uniform clinical manifest is required.

The Table 8 lib sheet uses MCI where its metadata and contrast labels use PCI. This label difference does not independently establish the same clinical diagnosis. The study reports blinding to codes for sequencing/analysis, but does not give a fully reconstructable phase-specific blinding and exclusion manifest.

Methods describe correlation/motif-based TF-peak-gene trios, SCENIC+ and inferred ligand/receptor communication. These are constructed associations, not selective regulator perturbations or measured cell-to-cell transmission. Negative TF-peak correlations are clipped in the trio score; its weights are not causal strengths.

Main Figure 2f-g caption and Table 11 title describe upregulated PCI accessibility targets, while adjacent main text describes downregulation. Main and Methods pathway counts also differ. Directional molecular mediation is not admitted while these discrepancies and unread table contents remain unresolved.

Reviewed material comprises main pages 1264-1267, Discussion on page 1272, Methods covering donors, nuclei isolation, sequencing and admitted analyses, Figure 2, Extended Data Figures 1 and 4 and all three reporting-summary pages. Main pages 1268-1271 and the remaining extended-data analyses were not fully reviewed.

Original Supplementary Tables 1 and 8 and the table legends were read; selected numeric cells and the complete sample/count census are checked locally. Other supplementary table contents were not audited. GEO GSE268609 is named by the paper, but its sample manifest and raw data were not obtained; no study-specific executable code was replayed.

The SA immature-cell comparison is significant against HA and AD, but not against YA or PCI at the table adjusted-P threshold of 0.05. These distinct contrasts neither prove no difference nor establish that generating neurons preserves memory.

studies.organism: Female mice labeled at five to seven weeks in Methods; six to seven weeks in Results
studies.preparation: Running-access mice with retroviral GFP or ChR2 labeling; cross-sectional bouton microscopy and later hippocampal slice optogenetics.
studies.observable: Bouton morphology, light-evoked spikes, postsynaptic currents and pharmacological response profiles.
studies.finding: Labeled granule-cell populations produce functional output in selected slices. Direct versus indirect routes and cross-sectional morphology constrain circuit hypotheses without establishing behavior or a unique construction sequence.
limitations: Female C57BL/6 mice received retrovirus at five to seven weeks in Methods, versus six to seven weeks in Results, after three to seven days of running-wheel access. Anatomy at 17, 28 and 75 days after labeling and later slice physiology are separate samples, not uniform mature-adult stages.

Functional recording covered 43 slices from 34 mice at 8.6-20.6 weeks after labeling. Fourteen responding target cells came from 11 slices of nine mice at 13.4-20.4 weeks. Most recordings used 200 micromolar BaCl2 to increase excitability and all-trans retinal to assist ChR2; these are not ordinary in vivo signaling conditions.

Broad illumination activates a labeled population, not a single presynaptic neuron. CAG-ChR2-GFP and PGK-ChR2-IRES-RFP are different constructs. ChR2 expression changes with age and affects spike latency and capture; normal-looking morphology is not an equivalence test for absence of opsin effects.

Of 107 sampled targets, 76 were classified as interneurons, 16 as mossy cells, 11 as pyramidal cells and four remained unclassified. Fourteen responded: 11 interneurons, one mossy cell, one CA3 pyramidal cell and one unclassified cell. This selected yield is not a connection probability. Supplementary Table 1 classification samples have different denominators.

Kynurenic acid blocks upstream glutamatergic transmission in direct and indirect routes. Bicuculline sensitivity in two of five tested targets supports a polysynaptic inhibitory component, including the illustrated CA3 pyramidal response; it does not establish direct newborn-neuron excitation of that pyramidal cell.

Seven of 14 responses were judged probably monosynaptic from kinetics, latency and pharmacology; two were probably polysynaptic and five were not resolved. Latency is measured from light onset, includes opsin-dependent presynaptic spiking and is not a directly measured synaptic delay or unique hop count.

Bouton selection requires size above three axon diameters, connection to an axon and isolation for tracing. Cross-sectional confocal and electron-microscopic samples do not trace bouton replacement over time or provide an unbiased population geometry. Mouse allocation and the mapping between contact-census and profile-analysis denominators are incomplete.

CA3 contact censuses at 17, 28 and 75 days use eight, eleven and twelve boutons; the largest-section analyses use seven, nine and ten. Di-aminobenzidine labeling can obscure vesicles. The active-zone omnibus P=0.12 coexists with a significant reported post hoc contrast; this does not support uniform growth across all measures.

Main captions label some ANOVA statistics as t; the main Methods specify Fisher PLSD after significant ANOVA whereas Supplementary Table 1 uses Tukey comparisons. One brain was excluded for insufficient labeling. Complete animal allocation, blinding, sample-size planning and raw-recording manifests are unavailable.

Main experimental text, Methods, Figures 1-5 and the complete four-page supplement were read; all main and supplementary figures and Table 1 were visually inspected. Raw recordings, animal-identified measurements and analysis code were not obtained or replayed.

The study measures morphology and output transmission, not behavior. Proposed recruitment of existing spines is a cross-sectional interpretation, not an observed minimal construction rule or proof of memory necessity.

studies.organism: Adult mixed-background mice; male-only fear tasks and separate reporter, irradiation and running cohorts
studies.preparation: Inducible Nestin-lineage Bax deletion, marker and BrdU assays, dentate field recordings and task-specific behavior; separate hippocampal irradiation.
studies.observable: Cell-label counts, proliferation markers, field LTP, contextual freezing discrimination, exploration and named null comparisons.
studies.finding: The Bax manipulation increases surviving cell labels and selected LTP and behavioral responses. It supports task-specific intervention effects, while unique mediation by neuron number and irradiation-based cognitive necessity remain unresolved.
limitations: NCff mice carry Nestin-CreERT2 and two floxed Bax alleles on a mixed C57BL/6-129/SvEv background. The primary contrast is tamoxifen versus vehicle within NCff, starting at at least eight weeks. Reporter NCY versus NCffY comparisons use separate littermate groups both receiving tamoxifen; Cre-negative Bax-floxed controls are another comparison.

The manipulation reduces Bax-dependent cell death in the Nestin stem/progenitor lineage; it is not a selective increase in birth rate or a dentate-newborn-neuron-only intervention. Olfactory-bulb survival also changes. Reporter recombination is a proxy, and altered cell properties or other lineage effects remain alternative mediators.

Behavioral testing is generally at 14-18 weeks with both sexes, but fear conditioning, discrimination, extinction and clearance use males. Experiments and analyses were blinded to genotype or treatment. A complete randomized allocation, exclusion, cage and prospective sample-size manifest is not reported.

The eight-week dentate BrdU assay labels on days 9-18 and counts on day 56; only a subset is NeuN-positive. Counts, marker fractions, proliferation and mature output are distinct. The olfactory and running BrdU schedules differ. Reporter neuron counts per section are not whole-dentate totals.

Weak-tetanus LTP is a population field response, not a birthdated single-cell recording. Eight-week assays without bicuculline use eight slices/six vehicle mice and eleven slices/seven tamoxifen mice; with bicuculline they use four slices/three vehicle and six slices/three tamoxifen mice. Slice-level statistics do not reconstruct animal-level independence.

Main Figure 2c alternates the order of contexts across days, whereas the discrimination Methods describe training context A followed one hour later by similar context B. The exact per-animal schedule requires reconciliation. The nine-day ratio analysis reports treatment P=0.023; its day F/degree-of-freedom/P combination also needs correction. Handling of a zero sum of freezing scores is unspecified.

Contextual freezing discrimination is a behavioral proxy for pattern separation, not a direct measurement of DG neural population codes or general memory improvement. Supplementary protocol variants have treatment P=0.38 and P=0.06 despite interactions or day-specific differences; they cannot be pooled as uniformly positive main effects.

Irradiation uses separate ten-week-old Bax-floxed mice and three 5 Gy exposures on days 1, 4 and 8, with behavior four months later. Regional irradiation is not a selective newborn-neuron ablation or a rescue experiment. Recall samples are eight sham/nine irradiated mice, versus seven/nine in discrimination; the missing sham inclusion is unresolved.

Supplementary Figure 14 reports an overall discrimination-ratio treatment P=0.1 and interaction P=0.3. Late within-group differences are not a between-group necessity test. Its day-five F(1,14)=4.34/P=0.04 pair needs reconciliation; no replacement biological P value is calculated here.

Running is a shared-cage exposure: two wheels for four to five mice, beginning five weeks after treatment. Figure 4 shows behavior on days 64-84. Individual running dose and cage independence are unresolved. Increased locomotion complicates an isolated anxiety interpretation, and home-cage activity has a separate sample.

Reported null outcomes are assay- and cohort-specific, not equivalence tests. Supplementary Figure 18 contains invalid negative F notation and conflicting novelty-suppressed-feeding significance; Figure 19 has a control-label conflict. Figure 20 contains a malformed marker percentage. These values are not silently corrected or admitted as quantitative defaults.

Granule-layer volume Methods and caption disagree on group size. Sholl analysis selects complex neurons and traces collapsed z-stacks; its null is not a unique three-dimensional geometry. Axon-length and cell-count cohorts cannot establish packing density or a complete output route without matched measurements.

Main experimental text and Methods, all four main figures, and the text of all 28 supplement pages were read. Supplementary pages 5, 16-19, 24 and 26-27 were visually inspected. Raw recordings, animal-level behavioral data and executable analysis code were not obtained or replayed.

Null object-recognition, water-maze, avoidance, extinction and clearance endpoints do not mean that every measured behavior is unchanged: the novel-object habituation locomotor interaction is significant. Multiple cohorts and distinct pre- and post-training manipulation schedules must remain separate.

studies.organism: One-month-old and older-than-four-month YFP-H mice
studies.preparation: Repeated transcranial two-photon imaging of superficial layer V apical dendrites during single-seed reaching or capellini handling, with separate naive, pretrained and control cohorts.
studies.observable: Interval-specific spine formation, elimination and survival; selected task success, functional maps and morphological null comparisons.
studies.finding: Novel motor training is accompanied by increased formation and elimination in selected cortical dendrites, and initially new spines are preferentially retained. The results constrain experience-dependent remodeling without proving a unique memory substrate or a universal construction law.
limitations: YFP-H mice were one month old or older than four months. Superficial apical dendrites of layer V pyramidal neurons were imaged 10-100 micrometers below the cortical surface under ketamine-xylazine anesthesia; these are selected cortical compartments, not a whole-brain connectome.

Main scientific text, Methods Summary and Figures 1-4 are reviewed. All text of the 12-page publisher supplement, Figures S1-S5 and Table S1 are reviewed, including visual inspection. The separate full Methods file and movie were not obtained or read; precise task procedures, sex, allocation, blinding and exclusions remain unverified.

Dense labeling prevented tracing complete individual neurons. The supplementary estimate of 20-80 sampled cells per mouse is not an identified neuron census. The study total of 32079 spines in 209 mice does not make spines independent animals or mean that every spine was followed for 120 days.

Formation and elimination are interval-specific percentages relative to the initial spine count. New-spine survival uses the newly appearing subset instead. These denominators cannot be exchanged or converted into universal growth rates, absolute density or graph weights.

General controls were littermates with the same food restriction and similar handling, without shaping or training. Learning, task exposure and reward are not individually isolated. Animal-level image stacks, cohort assignments and analysis code were not obtained; published tests were not independently reproduced.

The Figure 1f first-session training group selected four mice with more than ten successes in thirty reaches. Figure 1g also plots animals with ten or fewer successes, so the correlation cohort is not this selected four-mouse group. Imaging occurred within one hour after the session, but the baseline was from the previous day; this interval does not timestamp each spine birth within an hour.

Behavioral curves, spine-turnover cohorts and follow-up cohorts have different animal counts. The survival design uses two classification images and a third follow-up at a selected interval; it is not one fully sampled trajectory through every plotted timepoint.

Figure 2c normalizes total spine number to the initial image. Both control and trained trajectories lie below their initial value by day 16. Convergence toward control levels is distinct from the abstract wording about return to the original level; no exact count setpoint or one-for-one replacement is demonstrated.

Spine morphology does not directly measure synaptic currents, presynaptic partner identity or memory content. The study does not selectively remove the retained spines to test memory necessity or uniquely assign different memories to disjoint synaptic sets.

Motor mapping was terminal in fourteen mice: five imaging regions lay within the forelimb map, six on its border and three outside but within 300 micrometers. The map was not followed longitudinally, and distance from its border does not identify a complete circuit or a construction geometry.

Named nonsignificant comparisons are not equivalence tests. The long-duration activity controls had marked attrition: only two mice still reached more than twenty times daily at day eight and one at day sixteen. They do not support a well-powered universal exclusion of motor activity.

Spine-size analysis used head diameter divided by adjacent shaft diameter in 29 surviving spines; the cited supplementary paragraph does not supply its animal count. This selected morphological ratio is neither absolute spine volume nor measured synaptic strength.

Persistence to the reported approximately 120-day follow-up is finite. Training for sixteen days followed by the long untrained interval does not demonstrate permanence, a globally minimal circuit or a unique homeostatic construction law.

studies.organism: Adult male C57BL6 YFP-H mice, approximately 2.5-7 months old
studies.preparation: Targeted sensorimotor photothrombosis or sham surgery; acute urethane-anesthetized cortical imaging in separate recovery cohorts, plasma labeling, sensory reflectance maps and terminal histology.
studies.observable: Six-hour spine formation and elimination, dendritic spine density, projected orientation, fluorescent vascular volume fraction, capillary velocity and sensory-evoked reflectance.
studies.finding: Selected peri-infarct samples show increased spine formation and altered morphology after photothrombosis. Recovery cohorts, optical readouts and spatial comparisons constrain injury-associated remodeling without proving behavioral restoration or a unique construction mechanism.
limitations: Adult male C57BL6 YFP-H mice were approximately 2.5-7 months old. Layer 5 neuronal apical tufts were sampled within the superficial 100 micrometers, typically 100-500 micrometers from the posterior-medial infarct edge; this is selected surviving cortex, not the whole injured brain.

Main scientific text, Materials and Methods, and Figures 1-5 with captions are reviewed. Supplemental Figures 1-2 were not obtained or read. Animal-identified image stacks, custom IgorPro routines and the allocation/exclusion manifest were not obtained; no imaging or biological experiment was independently reproduced.

Photothrombosis used Rose Bengal 100 milligrams per kilogram intraperitoneally and 532-nanometer illumination, 17 milliwatts for fifteen minutes, under ketamine-xylazine. Sham controls omitted either dye or illumination. Per-assay sham composition, random allocation and group-specific age distributions are not supplied in the reviewed account.

Imaging under urethane was acute: hourly stacks over six, occasionally seven hours, after a one-, two- or six-week recovery interval, followed by terminal histology. Separate cohorts do not trace the same spine or dendritic arbor continuously from before injury through six weeks.

Only laterally projecting spines were scored. New spines had to protrude at least four pixels, approximately 0.55 micrometers, and remain present at the six-hour endpoint. Transient events, filopodium conversions, shifted segments and poor-quality images were excluded. The assay is not a census of all spine births, losses or synapses.

Turnover is reported as a percentage of the counted spine population over the imaging session; raw animal-level numerator/denominator assignments are unavailable. Spine density is a count per ten micrometers of dendrite. Neither measure is a neuron birth rate, a universal hourly turnover constant or a calibrated graph weight.

Turnover scoring was blinded to experimental condition, but movement, abnormal breathing and image deterioration could exclude experiments; exclusion counts and animal identifiers are not supplied. Axial optical resolution was about 5.3 micrometers, much poorer than lateral resolution, and six spine-appearance cases were pooled across animals for shaft-fluorescence controls.

Spine morphology and adjacent sensory-evoked reflectance do not measure the functional efficacy of each new synapse, selective memory content or behavioral recovery. The Discussion explicitly leaves the causal link between increased formation and recovered function unestablished.

The main text gives a 0.14 percent control formation mean and 1.37, 0.93 and 0.75 percent poststroke means. The abstract describes a five- to eight-fold peak increase; these rounded quantities do not define one exact fold estimate. Retain the reported assay means without calibrating a universal multiplier.

The six-week density cohort reports five mice versus six controls but t(8)=1.43, P=0.09. The three-mouse near/far comparison reports t(3)=4.87, P<0.01 for formation and t(3)=1.92, P=0.08 for elimination. Sidedness and statistical units need resolution before numerical reproduction; these degrees of freedom do not establish an ordinary paired three-mouse test.

Orientation uses projected 15-30 micrometer segments, eighteen ten-degree bins, and three mice per group, with the infarct placed at a common reference position. Reported F(17,17) tests concern bin-distribution variance; bins are not independent mice and this is not an animal-level circular-statistical reconstruction.

The authors consider mechanical distortion during tissue loss and scar formation as well as growth and retraction. Projected dendrite-vessel alignment does not isolate shared guidance, establish physical contact or prove an optimal generative network geometry.

Texas Red dextran labels plasma. Capillary velocity in micrometers per second is distinct from volumetric perfusion; fluorescent vessel volume fraction is distinct from vessel number, connectivity and selectively demonstrated angiogenesis. The vascular cohort totals fourteen animals but per-timepoint assignments and segmentation routines remain unresolved.

The near/far spine comparison uses approximately 0.33 versus 1.65 millimeters from the infarct edge at two weeks. This is different from the orientation comparison of less than 250 versus 500-800 micrometers at six weeks. Restricted ipsilateral sampling does not establish absence of remodeling elsewhere.

Nonsignificant outcomes are not equivalence or full recovery. Photothrombosis does not permit controlled reperfusion, and the paper does not directly establish the same time course in other stroke models, traumatic injury or humans.

studies.organism: Human autopsy tissue; five BrdU-labeled cancer patients aged 57-72 years at death and one uninfused staining control
studies.preparation: Diagnostic BrdU exposure followed by postmortem hippocampal and subventricular histology; neuronal and glial immunostains, confocal and brightfield controls.
studies.observable: Retained BrdU labeling, marker colocalization and sampled regional cell densities across different patients.
studies.finding: Dentate BrdU-positive cells include cells with neuronal markers. The clinical sampling, labeling assumptions and lack of functional assays limit birth-rate, lifespan and circuit-integration conclusions.
limitations: Five cancer patients received diagnostic BrdU labeling; one patient with similar cancer and no BrdU served as a staining control. This is an observational autopsy series, not a randomized intervention on neurogenesis or a healthy-population survey.

Figure 2 pairs ages at death of 72, 58, 57, 68 and 67 years with 16, 136, 274, 393 and 781 days after infusion. Different people supply the intervals; their bars are not longitudinal survival measurements of one cohort or an age-controlled birth-rate curve.

A single intravenous infusion contained 250 mg BrdU in 100 ml saline. No anticancer therapy was given before or during labeling and no cerebral metastases were found at autopsy. Later treatment, full clinical histories, sex-specific sampling, postmortem intervals and selection or exclusion counts are not reconstructable from the report.

BrdU marks DNA synthesis and subsequent label retention. The neuronal-marker interpretation supports candidate adult-born cells under the labeling assumptions; the images do not continuously observe cell division, trace a clone or selectively exclude every nonmitotic DNA-synthesis mechanism.

NeuN, NSE and calbindin were alternative neuronal stains with BrdU and GFAP, not three independent birthdating assays or necessarily three labels on each same cell. Reported neuronal percentages use BrdU-positive cells as denominator, not all neurons. At least twenty BrdU-positive cells per patient were examined; exact marker-specific denominators and patient-level counts are unavailable.

Figure 1e caption mixes human and rat descriptions; panel-specific species identity remains unresolved.

studies.finding: The isotope profiles support postnatal DNA synthesis under the birthdating assumptions. limitations: The accepted supplement starts with 156 fractions (74 NeuN-positive and 82 NeuN-negative), retains 55 and 65 for isotope analysis, and uses 51 and 64 for individual 2POP fits after four neuronal and one nonneuronal exclusions. Paired analyses use 40 pairs. These are different analysis populations, not 120 independent donors.

This is an observational autopsy study, not a randomized neurogenesis intervention. Main text gives ages 19-92, but accepted Table S1 includes NeuN-negative pub_id 53 aged 16.2. Table S1 also contains pre-2000 death dates despite the stated 2000-2012 tissue procurement interval. Donor identity, procurement chronology, clinical selection, exclusions and the final sample manifest need reconciliation.

Accepted Table S1 gives different birth-date/age entries for the two fractions labeled pub_id 49, while neuronal pub_id 69 and nonneuronal pub_id 68 share displayed age, birth/death dates and sex. Neither identical metadata nor matching pub_id alone establishes the complete paired donor manifest.

AMS measures bulk genomic-DNA carbon-14, reported as fraction modern or decay-corrected delta carbon-14. These are isotope concentrations, not counts of new neurons or single-cell birth timestamps. The method integrates DNA synthesis under assumptions about atmospheric carbon and the food chain.

NeuN sorting separates marker-positive nuclei from a heterogeneous marker-negative fraction, which includes several glial and vascular-associated cell types. Representative Figure S1 purities are not the purity of every sample; Table S1 includes neuronal sorting purity of 79%. Linear mixture correction does not independently validate cell lineage, and nonneuronal NA fields are not zero contamination.

AMS was blinded to sample age and origin. This does not establish blinding of all collection, selection or modeling. The main instrumental error description does not replace the sample-specific SD columns. Accepted Table S1 includes unresolved SD entries, such as F14C SD 1.01 alongside delta carbon-14 SD 14.00 for neuronal pub_id 21; values have not been silently corrected.

The birthdating interpretation assumes stable DNA after the last division and new cells arising from an actively proliferating progenitor pool. DNA synthesis is not a continuously observed division or clone. An old postmitotic reservoir migrating into the tissue was not modeled; the discussion of DNA repair includes unpublished stroke observations and does not selectively test every alternative.

Whole hippocampi were analyzed; the investigators could not separately radiocarbon-date hippocampal subdivisions. Dentate localization and absolute cell-number scaling rely on other histological and stereological studies. The approximately 700 neurons per day in each hippocampus and 0.004% of dentate neurons per day are model-dependent estimates, not directly counted daily births.

Global neuronal 2POP fitting reports a renewing fraction near 0.35, with a reported 95% interval of 0.12-0.63. For nonneuronal cells the main text reports 0.51 with interval 0.22-0.88, accepted Table S2 gives 0.56, and individual fits fix 0.55. These summaries must not be treated as one exactly reproduced estimate.

The reported individual medians, 1.75% per year for neurons and 3.5% for nonneuronal cells, apply within fixed renewing fractions of 0.35 and 0.55 after the stated exclusions. Global-fit rates of about 12% and 4.9% per year in Tables S3 and S2 are different estimands. Unfittable samples were excluded from the individual 2POP analysis; Figure 2C/5A additionally states plot limits below 0.001 or above 1.5.

The accepted supplement distinguishes unpaired 2POP comparison (51 neuronal and 64 nonneuronal fractions, rank-sum P=0.005) from 40 matched pairs (signed-rank P=0.054; neuronal median 1.5%, nonneuronal 3.5% per year). The latter null does not establish equal rates. Comparing these tests without their populations and denominators would be misleading.

Age associations use cross-sectional, model-derived rates: reported neuronal r=-0.31, P=0.03 and nonneuronal r=-0.35, P=0.04. They do not trace the same people over time or identify an age intervention. The sex comparison P=0.41 does not establish equivalence. The DCX overlay uses an external Knoth cohort, not birthdating of the same cells.

The accepted supplement prints a heuristic labeled AIC, p + log2(SSE), and requires a halving of SSE per added parameter. Applying that printed rule to rounded Table S2 gives 0.31 > 0.51/2, so its nonneuronal 2POP preference does not follow from that rule. Table S3 has 0.17 < 0.49/2 for neurons. This arithmetic checks reporting consistency only; final supplementary methods, likelihood and code remain unverified.

The source says subjects born around 1955-1965 discriminate 2POP from homogeneous age-dependent alternatives; without them the scenarios could not be distinguished. MCMC explores bounded parameter sets, and fitting several scenarios does not prove a unique biological mechanism. Full numerical replay and out-of-sample discrimination have not been performed.

The fitting procedure assumes a one-year food lag and development beginning six months before birth. Its weighted SSE squares weights of 1 or 2 assigned around a 10-microgram carbon boundary. Table S1 has both estimated DNA carbon mass and reactor-measured mass, including ND entries. The exact mass choice, boundary treatment and missing-value policy require executable code before reproducing the fit.

Figure 6 illustrates 2POPEd with initial renewing fraction 0.31, nonrenewing death rate 0.0035 per year, newborn death rate 0.11 per year and death-rate half-reduction age 19 years. The chosen set belongs to the best 3% of 300,000 explored sets; it is not a uniquely identified law. The reported 7.1-year half-life and external stereological age profiles are model-linked summaries, not longitudinal tracking of those human neurons.

The supplement explicitly does not explore population feedback: birth and death rates do not depend on the population state. Constant population size in replacement scenarios is imposed by their birth boundary, not observed emergence of a stabilizing rule. Population turnover does not identify one-for-one functional replacement, circuit topology or a universal minimal assembly.

No human electrical, identified synaptic-output or selective behavioral assay is performed. Similar estimated rates across species do not supply human functional integration or a birth-to-cognition mechanism. Histology, isotope dating, molecular markers and rodent interventions remain distinct evidence.

studies.organism: Adult rhesus and cynomolgus macaques, both sexes, 5.5-16.5 years; assay-specific animal allocation is unresolved
studies.preparation: Single or five daily intravenous BrdU injections, separate postmortem PCNA, neuronal fluorescence and oligodendroglial peroxidase assays in hippocampal tissue.
studies.observable: Regional BrdU and PCNA profiles; BrdU colabeling with NeuN or TuJ1, and with O4 or CNP; separate conditional numerical and lineage interpretations.
studies.finding: The reported marker combinations support adult macaque dentate neuronal and oligodendroglial production under the labeling assumptions. They do not identify a universal rate, common multipotent founder, observed migration, replacement feedback or cognitive function.
limitations: Ten adult macaques of both sexes include Macaca mulatta and Macaca fascicularis, aged 5.5-16.5 years. The paper does not provide an animal-by-species, sex, age, dosing, survival and assay manifest. Ten injected animals do not establish ten independent animals for every neuronal or glial endpoint.

Intravenous BrdU was 50 mg/kg, either once or daily for five consecutive days, administered between 09:00 and noon. Materials and Methods lists survival times ending at 72 days, whereas Results twice gives 75 days as the maximum. The reference injection for that discrepancy is not reconciled; neither value is silently selected.

BrdU and PCNA label DNA synthesis or cell-cycle-associated profiles; they do not continuously observe completed cytokinesis or a clone. PCNA was examined in sections from the same brains, not as a second independent animal cohort or a reported same-cell BrdU/PCNA lineage assay. Apposed doublets suggest, but do not identify, sibling relationships.

Early and later regional labeling is compared across sacrificed animals. BrdU-positive cells at the longest interval are not specifically identified as neurons. Label retention does not establish the survival fraction of a birth cohort, a neuron-specific lifespan, absence of rapid turnover elsewhere or absence of BrdU toxicity.

Neuronal double labeling was examined 32 days after the last of five injections in PFA-fixed 40-micrometre cryosections. Twenty nonadjacent sections were examined for each of NeuN and TuJ1; these are section counts, not independent animals. Exact biological replication, section sampling, denominators and uncertainty are not supplied for the reported averages.

BrdU/NeuN and BrdU/TuJ1 are alternative marker assays, not a reported three-marker identity for every labeled cell. The study reports neuronal colabels in GCL/SGZ and none in the other examined hippocampal regions; sampling and marker sensitivity do not establish absolute regional absence. Raw confocal stacks, optical section positions and segmentation have not been reanalysed.

Fluorophore reversal, omitted-primary controls and Figure 2c-d address staining and channel artifacts. They do not establish lineage, complete specificity or quantified sensitivity. Antibody omission is not a biological no-neurogenesis control, and no matched dose-control experiment establishes BrdU safety.

O4 or CNP double labeling used sequential black nuclear and brown cytoplasmic peroxidase signals in ethanol-fixed paraffin sections of 8 or 10 micrometres. Figure 3 shows 27-day single-injection examples. These preparations are distinct from the 32-day neuronal fluorescence assay; marker-positive morphology does not measure myelin formation or conduction.

Astrocyte generation is attributed to Eckenhoff and Rakic (1988) and Eriksson et al. (1998), not a newly reported GFAP assay in this experiment. Finding several phenotypes near one niche does not establish a shared multipotent founder, self-renewal or exclusive stem-cell lineage. The 1988 GFAP/autoradiographic assays are separately reviewed and do not trace a common founder.

The approximately 1,000 BrdU/TuJ1-positive cells per hippocampus is extrapolated from about two profiles per section, 40-micrometre sections and an approximately 19-mm external anatomical length. Scaling by an external 4.8-million-neuron estimate and dividing by five injections gives the provisional 0.004% per day. This is not a direct daily birth count or an unbiased whole-hippocampus stereological census.

Five-day cumulative labeling followed by 32 days of survival combines labeling opportunity, subsequent division, dilution, survival and marker expression. A single retained-label estimate does not identify production and death separately. The paper itself leaves lower production versus lower survival unresolved. No empirical edge weight or universal rate is assigned.

The roughly tenfold rodent comparison uses a separate published mouse study and external denominators. The paper acknowledges unmatched age, species, environment, labeling and survival procedures. Absolute-age and relative-age hypotheses were not compared in one matched design, and this series supplies no invariant primate-to-human scaling.

Bipolar morphology and radial or tangential orientation support a migration interpretation but do not track displacement, origin or a radial-glial guidance interaction. Nearby cells are not a clone, and anatomical resemblance to developing neurons is not an executed construction rule.

The replacement interpretation draws on separate human neuron counts and macaque synapse counts. Synapse-count stability is not a matched neuron census. This experiment measures neither paired births and deaths, feedback of population state, replacement identity nor the fraction of older neurons ultimately renewed.

No electrical, synaptic-output, learning or memory assay was performed. A possible cognitive role, stable-memory benefit or recovery mechanism remains untested. Labeling in this study does not require an injury or learning manipulation and does not validate the source card's necessary incoming assertions, weights or minimum carrier counts.

Untrained controls retain labeled cells, and the authors leave unspecified natural learning as a possible contributor to baseline survival. limitations: Twelve rhesus monkeys were labeled at reported ages of six months to eleven years; Table 1 gives ages at death of seven months to seventeen years. One to seven injections of tritiated thymidine were given at 10 mCi/kg. This is radioactivity per body mass, not the later BrdU mass dose. The injection route is not stated. The narrative survival range is three days to more than six years; the table includes 6.3 years. Repeated exposures and long retention windows are not independent animals or instantaneous birth rates.

Table 1 describes six-digit dates as day/month/year, although entries such as 013183 require month/day/year. Under that interpretation case 11 ends with injection 011976 and death 012376, four elapsed days rather than the printed fourteen. Case 7 gives 043069 to 050269, two elapsed days versus three printed; inclusive dating may matter. The original dates and intervals remain unreconciled.

Between 500 and 1000 sections per animal were screened across major brain regions and spinal cord, followed by brightfield or Nomarski examination with a 63x oil objective. The estimated million cells per specimen is not an exact neuronal denominator, random whole-brain census or statistical upper bound on rare births. Table 1 specifies 8-micrometre sections and every second to tenth section depending on region size.

Heavy labeling was calibrated separately in each case from glial, endothelial or peripheral cells, usually more than 15-30 silver grains per nucleus. Light-microscopic autoradiography exposure was 12-18 weeks and electron-microscopic exposure exceeded 24 weeks. A common fixed threshold cannot be imposed retrospectively. Occasional neuronal profiles with fewer than five or six grains were not classified as newborn; artifact or DNA repair was proposed without a repair assay.

Nine animals were pregnant at injection; neuronal labeling in offspring served as a positive control. Peripheral renewing tissues were also examined. The offspring and tissue checks demonstrate label incorporation under their conditions; they do not establish complete sensitivity for rare adult neuronal births. Pregnancy and assay allocation by animal are unavailable.

Figure 1D-E and Figure 2 use a seven-month-old animal, with Figure 2 explicitly labeled at six months. These images are juvenile examples. Oligodendroglial labels were mostly reported at six and eighteen months, with only occasional postpubertal examples. Selected dentate GFAP and ultrastructural analysis is described without a complete case-by-assay manifest or independent neuronal-marker panel.

limitations: Eighteen rhesus monkeys span E140 to seventeen years: seventeen receive autoradiography and one E144 animal is used only for electron-microscopic GFAP. Table 1 contains four adult animals aged five, ten, ten and seventeen years at collection. Their seven, three, five and one injections total sixteen exposures, not sixteen independent animals.

Methods specifies six early developmental animals with one intravenous 5-10 mCi/kg tritiated-thymidine injection and one-hour survival. Table 1 instead prints one day for these rows. The eleven additional animals are described as surviving five weeks to two years, while Table 1 includes fourteen days, three years and six years. No adult one-hour cohort is documented; early developmental sampling cannot supply an adult short-interval null.

For adult cases 112883, 012980, 012376 and 021583, ages, injection counts and survival correspond to Rakic (1985) cases 12, 10, 11 and 8. This is evidence of overlapping material, pending original identity confirmation. Shared juvenile identifiers also have discordant age/survival reporting: 030783 is P149-P184 here versus seven months at death in 1985; 031683 is P507-P549 and six weeks here versus nineteen months and thirty-five days. Neither independent pooling nor silent record merging is justified.

Left hemispheres were sectioned at 8 micrometres and exposed for 10-18 weeks. Heavy light-microscopic labeling is more than half the maximum grain count in the most intensely labeled cells of each case. Electron microscopy uses four nuclear grains under low-background conditions. These distinct assay thresholds must not be merged with each other or with the 1985 threshold.

GFAP immunochemistry uses 30-micrometre vibratome sections from five animals. Antibody penetration reaches only about three micrometres. The normal-goat-serum primary-antibody control is incubated at 4 degrees C, whereas primary antiserum incubation is at room temperature. A negative GFAP profile need not be a neuron; technical false negatives and other glial or precursor identities remain possible.

Postnatal short-interval and longer-survival groups contain different animals. Approximately 150 sections across three longer-survival ages yielded eight profiles classified morphologically as definitive granule neurons, only one in P90-P155. These are sampled profiles, not eight animals, a clonal lineage or a daily birth rate; Nissl morphology has acknowledged identity limits.

The P149-P184 interval is thirty-five days/five weeks in Table 1 and text, but Figure 4B says six weeks. Figure 5 uses P507-P549. Neither is an adult cohort. The five-year-old seven-injection animal has about two labeled profiles per ten sections at three months, all small SGZ profiles without typical neuronal morphology. The seventeen-year-old animal retains a label given six years earlier; collection age does not date a new division at seventeen.

GFAP composition in Figures 7-10 concerns small SGZ cells without birth-label selection. The E144 animal was never thymidine-labeled; about half its sampled small cells are GFAP-positive. Approximately 75% at six months and a majority at later ages do not quantify the astrocytic fraction of adult newborn cells or prove two founder lineages.

The combined electron-microscopic assay examined 120 ultrathin semiserial sections from selected areas in each of three animals aged six months, one and a half years, and five years. A dozen reliably radiolabeled cells were found, six GFAP-positive. This is a pooled three-age subset, not twelve adult neurons or a representative adult astrocyte fraction. Figure 11 is juvenile; Figure 12 is the five-year-old animal.

Figure 12B is described as an oligodendroglial type in Results but as resting microglia in the caption. Its specific subtype remains unresolved. No labeled profile had reported neuronal ultrastructure or synapses in the examined sections; this sampling-limited null does not prove absence of all neuronal precursor potential.

The discussion calls sixteen injections to four adult animals equivalent to independent labeling experiments. Repeated exposures share animals and cumulative label windows. The eleven-of-twelve-month coverage is also pooled across animals and ages, not a matched adult seasonal experiment. No formal rare-neuron detection bound or exact cessation age is calculated.

No lineage tracing identifies whether phenotypes arise from separate committed founders or a common multipotent founder. The discussion allows other glial lines, undifferentiated cells and potential neuronal differentiation under other conditions. Regional co-occurrence and GFAP phenotype cannot close a precursor-to-neuron construction rule.

Gliogenesis, replacement and stable-neuron memory roles are interpretations. No paired birth/death census identifies population feedback, and no functional or behavioral test establishes that neuron turnover impairs memory. The adult autoradiographic null remains distinct from a universal prohibition on adult neurogenesis.

Figure 6 models population maintenance and possible radial/nonradial lineage relations. Matching requires a significant paired baseline comparison for observation and execution of the same action, with no corresponding control response.
