comparisons.candidate: Parallel dendritic and vascular orientation identifies a common generative wiring program.
comparisons.alternative: Mechanical deformation during tissue loss and scarring, independent growth or mixed mechanisms produce the observed alignment.
comparisons.discriminator: Follow three-dimensional tissue landmarks, neuronal and vascular identities, and candidate growth/mechanical perturbations with prespecified alternative predictions.
comparisons.limit: Cross-sectional projected angles and vascular volume fraction do not identify the cause of alignment or a unique minimal circuit.

comparisons.candidate: Human birth-labeled cells integrate electrically and contribute to cognition.
comparisons.alternative: Histological neuronal identity is present without demonstrated functional incorporation or measurable cognitive contribution.
comparisons.discriminator: Combine independent birthdating and cell identity with human functional measurements; test selective contribution before assigning mediation.
comparisons.limit: Human marker colocalization and radiocarbon dating come from different autopsy series. Neither measures input, output or behavior; fitted renewal and mouse preparations cannot replace the missing human assay.

comparisons.candidate: A discrete renewing/nonrenewing partition uniquely explains the human isotope observations.
comparisons.alternative: Other age-dependent or heterogeneous renewal processes remain compatible with the sampled isotope signal.
comparisons.discriminator: Reproduce the full sample and error model, resolve the printed selection criterion, and compare prespecified competing processes using independent observations and birth-year sensitivity.
comparisons.limit: The accepted supplement prints a heuristic labeled AIC, p + log2(SSE), and requires a halving of SSE per added parameter. Applying that printed rule to rounded Table S2 gives 0.31 > 0.51/2, so its nonneuronal 2POP preference does not follow from that rule. Table S3 has 0.17 < 0.49/2 for neurons. This arithmetic checks reporting consistency only; final supplementary methods, likelihood and code remain unverified. The source says subjects born around 1955-1965 discriminate 2POP from homogeneous age-dependent alternatives; without them the scenarios could not be distinguished. MCMC explores bounded parameter sets, and fitting several scenarios does not prove a unique biological mechanism. Full numerical replay and out-of-sample discrimination have not been performed.

comparisons.candidate: State-dependent feedback generates a stable renewing cell population and its circuit geometry.
comparisons.alternative: Population size follows an imposed replacement boundary or externally specified birth and death schedules.
comparisons.discriminator: Measure how population state changes birth and death hazards, compare feedback and externally imposed schedules, and test connection identity and functional consequences.
comparisons.limit: The supplement explicitly does not explore population feedback: birth and death rates do not depend on the population state. Constant population size in replacement scenarios is imposed by their birth boundary, not observed emergence of a stabilizing rule. Population turnover does not identify one-for-one functional replacement, circuit topology or a universal minimal assembly.

comparisons.candidate: Retained BrdU/TuJ1 profiles identify daily neuron production and a fixed cross-species rate ratio.
comparisons.alternative: Labeling coverage, survival, repeated division, marker expression and external denominators also determine the retained profiles.
comparisons.discriminator: Recover animal-identified stereological counts and labeling kinetics, measure production and survival separately, and compare species with matched age and protocols.
comparisons.limit: Five-day cumulative labeling followed by 32 days of survival combines labeling opportunity, subsequent division, dilution, survival and marker expression. A single retained-label estimate does not identify production and death separately. The paper itself leaves lower production versus lower survival unresolved. No empirical edge weight or universal rate is assigned. The roughly tenfold rodent comparison uses a separate published mouse study and external denominators. The paper acknowledges unmatched age, species, environment, labeling and survival procedures. Absolute-age and relative-age hypotheses were not compared in one matched design, and this series supplies no invariant primate-to-human scaling.

comparisons.candidate: One self-renewing multipotent founder generates the neuronal and glial phenotypes near the adult SGZ.
comparisons.alternative: Distinct committed progenitors generate phenotypes in the same niche.
comparisons.discriminator: Trace individual founders and complete progeny over time, including self-renewal, neuronal and glial identities; control clone collisions and sampling.
comparisons.limit: Astrocyte generation is attributed to Eckenhoff and Rakic (1988) and Eriksson et al. (1998), not a newly reported GFAP assay in this experiment. Finding several phenotypes near one niche does not establish a shared multipotent founder, self-renewal or exclusive stem-cell lineage. The 1988 GFAP/autoradiographic assays are separately reviewed and do not trace a common founder.

comparisons.candidate: New neurons follow an SGZ-to-GCL path guided by radial glial processes.
comparisons.alternative: Static cell shape and location arise without the proposed trajectory or guidance mechanism.
comparisons.discriminator: Track identified birthdated cells through time and selectively perturb the proposed guidance interaction while measuring viability and displacement.
comparisons.limit: Bipolar morphology and radial or tangential orientation support a migration interpretation but do not track displacement, origin or a radial-glial guidance interaction. Nearby cells are not a clone, and anatomical resemblance to developing neurons is not an executed construction rule.

comparisons.candidate: New neurons replace older neurons through feedback that preserves population size and memory.
comparisons.alternative: Addition, loss or externally regulated turnover can yield similar cross-sectional counts without identity-preserving replacement.
comparisons.discriminator: Measure identified births, deaths and population counts in the same macaque preparation, perturb population state and test matched circuit and memory consequences.
comparisons.limit: The replacement interpretation draws on separate human neuron counts and macaque synapse counts. Synapse-count stability is not a matched neuron census. This experiment measures neither paired births and deaths, feedback of population state, replacement identity nor the fraction of older neurons ultimately renewed. No electrical, synaptic-output, learning or memory assay was performed. A possible cognitive role, stable-memory benefit or recovery mechanism remains untested. Labeling in this study does not require an injury or learning manipulation and does not validate the source card's necessary incoming assertions, weights or minimum carrier counts.

comparisons.candidate: The oldest animals generate differentiated new granule neurons.
comparisons.alternative: Old-age proliferation and immature phenotype need not belong to one completed neuronal lineage.
comparisons.discriminator: Match initial division, later neuronal phenotype and retained-cell identity in the same aged preparation.
comparisons.limit: Methods explicitly states that two hours permits S-phase labeling but not completed mitosis or migration. All three 23-year-old animals have only this two-hour interval. The reported oldest-age BrdU and TOAD-64 profiles do not establish birthdated neuronal differentiation at that age. The PMC HTML Table 2 lists M. fascicularis group sizes of 4 young, 4 middle-aged and 2 aged, plus 2 middle-aged M. mulatta. These total 12 rather than the 11 Table 1 animals; Table 1 instead has 2 young and 3 aged animals. The reported F(2,5)=154.2 cannot be reproduced from an identified animal-level analysis. Printed-PDF agreement with the HTML table has not been verified.

comparisons.candidate: The two macaque studies identify a common quantitative production rule.
comparisons.alternative: Different labeling and survival windows can yield different retained-label counts without conflicting on neuronal phenotype.
comparisons.discriminator: Match species, age, dose, route, marker, survival and stereological denominators before comparing birth and survival estimates.
comparisons.limit: This study and Kornack and Rakic (1999) use different doses, routes, survival schedules, marker assays and counting procedures. Agreement on some neuronal colabels does not make their numerical rates or age groups interchangeable. The reviewed 1985/1988 autoradiographic protocols differ in sampling and phenotype criteria; matched detection sensitivity remains unresolved.

comparisons.candidate: Glucocorticoids cause the age-related marker decline.
comparisons.alternative: Other age-related processes and sampling differences explain the marker association.
comparisons.discriminator: Measure hormone exposure and manipulate its pathway with age-matched birthdated lineage and survival readouts.
comparisons.limit: Cortisol, learning, stress, enrichment and functional circuit activity were not measured or manipulated. The discussion draws on other species and publications to propose survival, glucocorticoid and memory mechanisms. It does not supply matched primate causal evidence or a universal prerequisite.

comparisons.candidate: The putative stream supplies functional adult olfactory neurons.
comparisons.alternative: Regional proliferating or immature profiles do not complete the proposed destination-specific lineage.
comparisons.discriminator: Trace division, movement, destination, phenotype and synaptic function in the same identified lineage.
comparisons.limit: BrdUrd profiles in a region corresponding to the rodent rostral migratory stream, occasional mitotic figures and TOAD-64 profiles motivate an olfactory-neuron interpretation. They do not track movement to the olfactory bulb, common ancestry, arrival, synaptic integration or sensory function.

comparisons.candidate: Training increases labeled cells exclusively by rescuing newborn neurons.
comparisons.alternative: Proliferation, label kinetics and other mediators can contribute to the retained-label difference.
comparisons.discriminator: Track identified birthdated cells across training, quantify division and death separately, and selectively perturb and rescue the proposed survival pathway.
comparisons.limit: The control time course rises from two hours to one week and falls by two weeks after labeling, but involves separate terminal cohorts. The survival interpretation also draws on prior autoradiographic grain counts and unpublished observations. The authors explicitly cannot exclude proliferation; a unique survival mechanism is not experimentally isolated. The late-labeling trace cohort receives BrdU on the final training day after learning criterion, followed by tissue collection 24 hours later. F(2,13)=0.011, P=0.9892 concerns that retained-label count, not every phase of proliferation throughout training or a direct instantaneous mitotic rate.

comparisons.candidate: Learning is a universal prerequisite for neurogenesis and new neurons are necessary for memory.
comparisons.alternative: Selected tasks modulate a labeled population without establishing either universal dependency.
comparisons.discriminator: Define the learning class and neuronal stage, then test selective loss and rescue with matched behavioral, birthdating and survival readouts.
comparisons.limit: Hippocampal dependence is imported from prior lesion literature and, for the exact rat trace protocol, unpublished lesion data. No matched hippocampal lesion or selective newborn-cell manipulation is performed in this histology study. The graph links the specified task protocol to its measured outcome, not generic hippocampal necessity. No newborn-cell necessity, selective rescue, synaptic-output or memory-storage test is performed. Untrained controls retain labeled cells, and the authors leave unspecified natural learning as a possible contributor to baseline survival. The study establishes neither a universal learning prerequisite nor its universal absence, and no primate or human generalization follows.

comparisons.candidate: Autoradiographic nulls and later BrdU neuronal colabels directly identify a single age-dependent production law.
comparisons.alternative: Age, dose, retention, processing, sampling and phenotype criteria differ across studies.
comparisons.discriminator: Match animal age at injection, species, label kinetics, survival, neuronal identity and detection sensitivity, then compare independent samples.
comparisons.limit: The reviewed observations differ across preparations. Neither a null-to-zero-rate inference nor an interchangeable quantitative BrdU/autoradiographic estimate is supported.

comparisons.candidate: Two papers and sixteen adult injections supply independent biological confirmations.
comparisons.alternative: Repeated injections share four adults, and the papers have matching specimen identifiers and schedules.
comparisons.discriminator: Reconcile original animal identities, dates and assay allocation; analyze repeated measures within animal and overlapping publications as dependent.
comparisons.limit: Adult case correspondences strongly indicate shared material; juvenile dates and ages conflict. Raw identity confirmation is unavailable, so the papers cannot be pooled as independent replications.

comparisons.candidate: Distinct neuronal and glial phenotypes establish separate committed founders or a single multipotent founder.
comparisons.alternative: Marker state and morphology are compatible with multiple ancestry models.
comparisons.discriminator: Trace individual founder ancestry and fate across the relevant developmental and adult intervals with independent phenotype validation.
comparisons.limit: No lineage tracing identifies whether phenotypes arise from separate committed founders or a common multipotent founder. The discussion allows other glial lines, undifferentiated cells and potential neuronal differentiation under other conditions. Regional co-occurrence and GFAP phenotype cannot close a precursor-to-neuron construction rule.

comparisons.candidate: No detected neuronal label establishes a universal developmental stop.
comparisons.alternative: Rare events or alternative detection/retention conditions can yield an observed null without a zero biological rate.
comparisons.discriminator: Define the sampled population, independent units, labeling efficiency and detection probability; estimate a justified bound and compare matched later observations.
comparisons.limit: Between 500 and 1000 sections per animal were screened across major brain regions and spinal cord, followed by brightfield or Nomarski examination with a 63x oil objective. The estimated million cells per specimen is not an exact neuronal denominator, random whole-brain census or statistical upper bound on rare births. Table 1 specifies 8-micrometre sections and every second to tenth section depending on region size. Methods specifies six early developmental animals with one intravenous 5-10 mCi/kg tritiated-thymidine injection and one-hour survival. Table 1 instead prints one day for these rows. The eleven additional animals are described as surviving five weeks to two years, while Table 1 includes fourteen days, three years and six years. No adult one-hour cohort is documented; early developmental sampling cannot supply an adult short-interval null. The discussion calls sixteen injections to four adult animals equivalent to independent labeling experiments. Repeated exposures share animals and cumulative label windows. The eleven-of-twelve-month coverage is also pooled across animals and ages, not a matched adult seasonal experiment. No formal rare-neuron detection bound or exact cessation age is calculated.

comparisons.candidate: Adult-born neurons contribute to pattern separation.
comparisons.alternative: Temporal association or memory resolution contributes to the observed behavior; these mechanisms may coexist.
comparisons.discriminator: In one defined preparation, measure input/output code overlap, temporal association and novel-feature retention with selective birth-cohort perturbations; specify distinct predictions before comparing models.
comparisons.limit: The reviews synthesize different preparations and illustrate hypotheses. Their schematics do not adjudicate this matched comparison; a successful discrimination task alone is insufficient.

comparisons.candidate: PV-dependent RGL regulation closes an adaptive circuit feedback loop.
comparisons.alternative: PV manipulation changes short-window stem-cell cycling without a compensating effect of new neurons on the original circuit variable.
comparisons.discriminator: Measure a declared circuit deviation, PV/GABA responses, identified RGL lineages and newborn-neuron integration longitudinally; selectively interrupt the new-neuron return path and test restoration of the original variable.
comparisons.limit: The published experiments do not measure this complete loop. The schematic and anatomical coverage cannot establish feedback closure, stability or a minimum carrier count.

comparisons.candidate: RGL gamma2-containing GABA receptors mediate the full effect of PV stimulation on stem-cell cycling.
comparisons.alternative: Indirect circuit effects and other niche signals contribute alongside the receptor-related response.
comparisons.discriminator: Cross matched PV stimulation with selective, verified RGL receptor perturbation and rescue; estimate the factorial interaction while measuring local GABA and the same cycle endpoints.
comparisons.limit: Conditional deletion, slice pharmacology and systemic diazepam responses support a receptor-related route but do not execute this selective PV-by-RGL mediation test. Descendant recombination, systemic effects and pairwise nulls leave alternatives open.

comparisons.candidate: One in vivo Sox2-positive founder combines serial self-renewal with neuronal and astrocytic output.
comparisons.alternative: Distinct lineage-restricted founders, spatial collisions or selection generate the separate terminal cluster patterns.
comparisons.discriminator: Combine unique founder labeling with longitudinal division and fate tracking; estimate collision, missed-descendant and survival rates within animal-identified lineages.
comparisons.limit: Sparse mixed clusters support conditional ancestry, but do not jointly trace repeated renewal and both differentiated fates from the same founder. Culture potency under separate conditions cannot complete that in vivo lineage.

comparisons.candidate: Regulated allocation of Sox2-positive descendants maintains the precursor population during increased production.
comparisons.alternative: Reporter kinetics, cell loss, sampling or group differences produce similar endpoint densities without a regulating feedback loop.
comparisons.discriminator: Resolve running-control genotypes, track total population and birth/loss trajectories with stable lineage labels, then perturb the proposed feedback variable and measure recovery.
comparisons.limit: Density nulls are not equivalence or population conservation; no complete matched birth/loss balance or controller is measured. Population-level asymmetric contribution does not imply asymmetric division.

comparisons.candidate: Radial and nonradial Sox2-positive states participate in a reversible, renewing lineage cycle.
comparisons.alternative: Distinct reservoirs, one-way production or morphological state changes account for the fixed-tissue patterns.
comparisons.discriminator: Track both transition directions and repeated divisions in the same identified founders while measuring reporter and morphology changes.
comparisons.limit: The radial-process cluster and depth series do not observe a conversion through time. Figure 6A marks unestablished transitions and supplies no measured cycle closure.

comparisons.candidate: Temporary multimodal binding uses a store distinct from activated long-term memory.
comparisons.alternative: Activated long-term memory with task-dependent attention accounts for the binding readout.
comparisons.discriminator: Match stimulus material, retention, binding, distraction and retrieval demands; compare selective perturbations and predicted cross-task transfer for the two models.
comparisons.limit: The review proposes the episodic buffer and discusses alternatives; no matched primary discrimination is admitted here.

comparisons.candidate: Robust goal-related maintenance requires local recurrent PFC activity.
comparisons.alternative: Cellular bistability or distributed recurrent loops support maintenance without the proposed local recurrent mechanism.
comparisons.discriminator: Define the task-relevant representation, delay and distractors; separately perturb intrinsic cellular persistence, local recurrence and interregional feedback while measuring maintenance and recovery. Test combinations where mechanisms can coexist.
comparisons.limit: Reviewed PF recordings, priority-dependent fMRI and post-TMS EEG constrain observable predictions but do not selectively isolate local recurrence, cellular persistence or distributed feedback. Category-level decoding and nulls cannot uniquely identify a carrier; mechanisms may coexist.

comparisons.candidate: Learned dopamine gating selectively updates maintained task context.
comparisons.alternative: Other circuit or plasticity mechanisms select updates without the proposed dopamine-mediated gate.
comparisons.discriminator: Measure reward, update timing and representational transitions; perturb the proposed gate selectively and compare learned updating and distraction resistance with explicit alternative models.
comparisons.limit: The conceptual learning account is not a reproduced algorithm or a measured, causally closed control loop. Monitoring, gating and plasticity require separate evidence.

comparisons.candidate: Post-TMS category evidence reflects reinstatement of the specific remembered item.
comparisons.alternative: TMS reinstates category context without recovering the specific item representation.
comparisons.discriminator: Decode held-out within-category item identity and relate it to trial-level recognition under matched sham, relevance and timing controls.
comparisons.limit: The admitted category decoder does not perform this item-level discrimination; the behavioral lure comparison uses a separate cohort without EEG.

comparisons.candidate: A silent synaptic trace stores the temporarily unattended information.
comparisons.alternative: Weak active, distributed or dynamic representations support later access without the proposed exclusively silent carrier.
comparisons.discriminator: Calibrate readout sensitivity and directly perturb or measure the proposed carrier while predicting item-specific recovery, including combinations of mechanisms.
comparisons.limit: No synaptic weights or unique carrier were directly measured. Category reactivation and global complexity nulls do not settle this mechanism.

comparisons.candidate: A nested constituent model explains the tested sequence behavior.
comparisons.alternative: Transitions, memorized chunks, ordinal associations or finite heuristics explain the same observations.
comparisons.discriminator: Hold out both items and structural depths; construct contrasts matched for timing, local statistics and memory demand, and compare predictive errors of explicit models.
comparisons.limit: This records a proposed discriminator. Review illustrations and a finite training set do not establish an unbounded grammar or a physical construction chain.

comparisons.candidate: A specified vector role-binding operation implements compositional representations.
comparisons.alternative: Other distributed, conjunctive or sequential mechanisms account for role-sensitive behavior and neural readouts.
comparisons.discriminator: Fit explicit binding and recovery models, test novel role/filler combinations and repeated fillers, and perturb predicted carriers while controlling general task impairment.
comparisons.limit: No reviewed primary preparation selectively identifies tensor binding or circular convolution; they are not interchangeable operations.

comparisons.candidate: Compact geometric programs predict perception and production across new forms.
comparisons.alternative: Learned visual representations, other grammars or combined models explain the tested performances.
comparisons.discriminator: Use separate model-selection and evaluation data, matched exposure and stimulus controls; compare recognition, generation and transfer, with measured human baselines for each task.
comparisons.limit: Recognition, generation and transfer have not received the comprehensive held-out comparison. Selected Pajot et al. deposited readouts are independently recomputed and show task-dependent symbolic contributions; its cross-format ideal rank remains theoretical. Neither fitted performance nor arithmetic reproduction identifies a unique neural code.

comparisons.candidate: Placeholder structures and analogical alignment support a change in the available conceptual repertoire.
comparisons.alternative: New associations, instructions or compositions within existing resources explain the apparent change.
comparisons.discriminator: Measure prior resources and intermediate symbol meanings longitudinally, manipulate the proposed learning inputs and test generalization to previously untrained relations.
comparisons.limit: Selected theoretical passages define the proposal; they do not supply a matched causal comparison or a formal proof of expressive non-definability.

comparisons.candidate: A noisy shortest-prefix program model predicts the observed within-sequence error pattern.
comparisons.alternative: Constant performance per sequence, distance summaries or other sequence learners account for the observations.
comparisons.discriminator: Reconcile the published grammar and feedback algorithm, reproduce participant-level fits, and compare fully specified models on held-out sequences and participants.
comparisons.limit: The published adult fit improves on the constant-per-sequence comparator over a range of noise values; the same full-language noise model poorly fits children and Munduruku participants. Grammar choices and fixed capacity are assumptions, not fitted neural measurements. These are published fits without independent reproduction.

comparisons.candidate: Reduced availability of nesting and point symmetry explains the group profiles.
comparisons.alternative: Full nesting with reduced point-symmetry use, memory demands, variable strategy or experience explains the profiles.
comparisons.discriminator: Recover the implementation, quantify competing fits, and test resource-specific predictions with matched memory demand and new stimuli rather than interpreting fitted group probabilities as individual capacities.
comparisons.limit: The child fit favors low nonzero availability over the illustrated full-language noise models. For Munduruku participants, full nesting with fitted point-symmetry availability yields a comparable fit. Setting both resources to zero fits poorly. This does not prove the absence or universal necessity of either resource.

comparisons.candidate: Formal schooling causes the observed difference in geometric-rule use.
comparisons.alternative: Age, task procedure, experience, memory demand and sampling contribute to the cohort differences.
comparisons.discriminator: Compare age- and procedure-matched participants with measured exposure, and use a suitable longitudinal or assigned educational intervention before making a causal schooling claim.
comparisons.limit: French college adults use a longer click task; children and Munduruku volunteers use a shorter pointing task with different preview exposure. The Munduruku sample combines 14 young participants and six adults and is not an isolated test of formal schooling.

comparisons.candidate: The specified minimum-description cost accounts for behavioral and anticipation differences.
comparisons.alternative: Primitive-specific difficulty, spatial distance and other learned sequence representations explain additional variation.
comparisons.discriminator: Reconcile the grammar and trial pipeline, fit explicit competing models with selection inside training folds, and test new sequences matched for distance and primitive composition.
comparisons.limit: Reported associations coexist with retained stimulus predictors, a null formal-cost association for location decoding and unverified printed minimum costs. No independently reproduced or held-out winner is established.

comparisons.candidate: The same primitive code generalizes from isolated rules to sequence contexts.
comparisons.alternative: Context-dependent representation or timing, head position and sensitivity differences prevent cross-task decoding.
comparisons.discriminator: Match timing and measurement geometry, counterbalance task order, compare explicit code transformations, and report cross-task sensitivity and equivalence bounds.
comparisons.limit: Within-part decoding is positive, but cross-part decoding/RSA and the sequence matched-pair test are nonsignificant. A null classifier does not establish a specific binding operation.

comparisons.candidate: A numerical ordinal code implements the repetition variable of the proposed program.
comparisons.alternative: Temporal phase, boundaries or other grouped sequential codes generate the observed readouts.
comparisons.discriminator: Vary tempo, group size and sequence length independently while testing transfer to new items and structures and selectively perturbing predicted carriers.
comparisons.limit: The experiment has fixed timing. Group-frequency and ordinal-label decoding constrain possible representations but do not distinguish numerical order from temporal position or identify a joint nested program.

comparisons.candidate: The specified IFG and mid-DLPFC effects isolate sequence complexity and nesting.
comparisons.alternative: Distance, memory, task demands, correlated regressors and ROI selection contribute to the observed maps.
comparisons.discriminator: Reconcile contrast weights and cohort membership, jointly compare explicit models with independent ROI selection, and measure sensitivity to control effects and selective perturbations.
comparisons.limit: Positive contrasts coexist with memory nulls and non-independent task ROI summaries. Exclusive masking and differently thresholded direct comparisons do not establish statistical independence or unique coding.

comparisons.candidate: A nested mental program generates the observed boundary behavior and neural patterns.
comparisons.alternative: Chunked transitions, motor anticipation and other learned sequential representations produce similar readouts.
comparisons.discriminator: Specify consistent sequence identities and parses, test new structures and timing, decode joint variables and selectively perturb predicted carriers while comparing explicit alternatives.
comparisons.limit: Behavioral fits, BOLD contrasts and grouping readouts constrain possible accounts but do not recover a unique joint program. The alternate templates and two-crosses nesting labels differ between the 2019 and 2021 studies.

comparisons.candidate: Spatial nested-rule processing can operate without natural-language circuitry.
comparisons.alternative: Shared or weakly active language-related resources contribute despite limited BOLD overlap.
comparisons.discriminator: Combine matched functional localizers and equivalence bounds with selective causal tests of task performance.
comparisons.limit: Observed localizer separation is not a necessity test; generally weak language ROI responses do not prove complete silence or absence of a contribution.

comparisons.candidate: The chosen repetition language captures structure used in binary sequence memory.
comparisons.alternative: Transition statistics, chunking, ordinal predictors and nonminimum parses explain overlapping aspects of behavior.
comparisons.discriminator: Reconcile the exact cost implementation and AIC table; compare explicit models on new templates with matched bracketing dimensions and held-out predictions.
comparisons.limit: The reported LoT-plus-surprise fit leads the tested candidates, but the Alternate bracketing prediction fails and surprise adds explanatory information. Neither result establishes a unique minimum program.

comparisons.candidate: A nested prefrontal program drives auditory predictions and deviant responses.
comparisons.alternative: Learned ordinal or chunked states and distributed task responses generate similar neural readouts.
comparisons.discriminator: Reproduce folds and acquisition membership, decode joint program variables on held-out structures, and selectively perturb predicted carriers under matched sensory and motor controls.
comparisons.limit: BOLD and MEG associations and violation-label decoding do not establish a directed generative circuit, unique grammar or minimum neural resources. Selected source reading is not raw-data reproduction.

comparisons.candidate: Binary sequence structure can be represented without natural-language circuitry.
comparisons.alternative: Language-related regions contribute alongside mathematics-associated and other task regions.
comparisons.discriminator: Use matched functional contrasts, equivalence bounds and selective causal tests of binary-sequence performance.
comparisons.limit: Localizer overlap is assay-dependent and has positive language-region exceptions. Weak average responses do not establish dispensability, and mathematical localizer overlap does not establish necessity.

comparisons.candidate: A chosen symbolic description supplies information complementary to visual-model distances.
comparisons.alternative: Visual readouts and selected image or task factors account for the behavioral fit without unique symbolic implementation.
comparisons.discriminator: Reconcile aggregation and participant inclusion; use matched layers and nested model selection, then test joint improvement on unseen shapes, grammars and human participants.
comparisons.limit: The quadrilateral conditional symbolic coefficient is nonsignificant, while the shape-memory joint fit is higher. Selected deposited arithmetic supports these distinct comparisons; in-sample fit does not establish held-out benefit or a unique neural program.

comparisons.candidate: Increasing training dataset size is itself the main cause of improved geometric performance.
comparisons.alternative: Training method, dataset content, architecture and selected layers contribute correlated differences.
comparisons.discriminator: Vary training sample size under matched architecture, objective, data distribution, evaluation stimuli and model-selection rules; separately measure human task performance.
comparisons.limit: The available-model comparison does not isolate training size. The dominant reported factor differs in the cross-format task, and its ideal benchmark supplies no human matching sample.

comparisons.candidate: Motor observation/execution matching is necessary for action recognition.
comparisons.alternative: Visual association and task-dependent sensorimotor responses permit recognition without a uniquely necessary matching mechanism.
comparisons.discriminator: Measure recognition behavior during selective perturbation with matched visual, motor, attention and action controls; compare the same preparation before generalizing across species.
comparisons.limit: Macaque F5 and human medial recordings show task-defined responses in different preparations. Neither performs the selective causal recognition test; human recordings include multiunit signals and clinically selected regions.

comparisons.candidate: The proposed functional components form a necessary and sufficient minimal empathy architecture.
comparisons.alternative: Different tasks recruit partly separable mechanisms for affect sharing, attribution, regulation and helping.
comparisons.discriminator: Operationalize each outcome and test selective perturbations, dissociations and matched alternatives; distinguish shared voxels from shared units and from shared experience.
comparisons.limit: The complete Decety and Jackson review explicitly treats the components as nonprimitive, distinguishes executive functions from mentalizing and describes heterogeneous outcome measures. The review and partner-pain imaging do not jointly establish a minimal architecture; perception, affect and working-memory claims need separate matched tests.

comparisons.candidate: Opposite observation/execution response directions implement motor suppression and self-other agency.
comparisons.alternative: Task-dependent sensorimotor responses and memory associations produce the patterns without a uniquely identified agency mechanism.
comparisons.discriminator: Measure agency judgments and motor output during selective perturbation with matched cue, effector, sensory-feedback and no-movement controls.
comparisons.limit: The sampled recordings contain no selective agency or motor-suppression intervention, and cannot calibrate a working-memory or empathy dependency.

comparisons.candidate: Shared self/partner-pain BOLD locations identify a common pain-specific affective neural representation.
comparisons.alternative: Partly distinct cells or codes and more general aversiveness, salience or attention account for spatial overlap.
comparisons.discriminator: Compare matched pain and nonpain aversive conditions, test cross-condition coding with independent data, and distinguish population imaging from common-cell evidence.
comparisons.limit: Singer cued partner-stimulation imaging and Tan picture-related iEEG are different assays. The latter arousal-correlation null is not an arousal-matched pain-specificity control; neither completes common-cell or cross-condition coding tests. Singer supporting methods remain unread.

comparisons.candidate: The eight removed decoding features define a minimal necessary neural construction for empathy.
comparisons.alternative: The ordered removal result depends on representation, correlated features, classifier and pooled stimulus sample.
comparisons.discriminator: Test alternative feature subsets and model families with participant and stimulus-pair blocking; separately test selective neural interventions against matched behavior.
comparisons.limit: The published removal path and selected saved arrays do not establish minimum cardinality, uniqueness, participant generalization or biological necessity.

comparisons.candidate: Regional detection order and directional coupling identify a causal information route through the four regions.
comparisons.alternative: Common inputs, shared references, frequency-dependent resolution and task-associated population dynamics account for the observed summaries.
comparisons.discriminator: Test selective perturbations with simultaneous regional readouts, matched references and filtering, patient-aware replication and explicit alternative causal models.
comparisons.limit: No selective neural perturbation is performed. Some sensitivity effects require relaxed thresholds, and channel pairs are not independent people.

comparisons.candidate: One general perception mechanism is necessary for all empathic understanding.
comparisons.alternative: Different perceptual, remembered, imagined and narrated inputs can support task-dependent social judgments.
comparisons.discriminator: Compare input modalities, memory and imagination in matched outcome tasks with selective perturbations and controls for instruction comprehension.
comparisons.limit: The review and the cued-stimulation and picture tasks do not selectively test a universal perceptual prerequisite or quantify its strength.

comparisons.candidate: General affect generation is a necessary mechanism for every form of social recognition and empathy.
